images.description: Construction continues on a redoubt. images.title: File:Flight 93 National Memorial - 20211226 - 14 - Visitor Center.jpg
images.description: The Visitor Center at the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania, as seen in December 2021. Designed by Paul Murdoch and the winner of the American Institute of Architects' award for Education Facility Design, the Flight 93 Memorial Visitor Center was described by the AIA as "a great example of poetic architecture in service of a central concept and experiential learning... beautiful in [its] representation of the story [it] tell[s]." Paradoxically, while the building is a focal point that's widely visible within the site itself (thanks to its prominent hilltop location), yet its design is unobtrusive and dutifully directs the visitor's attention back to the Memorial Plaza, Wall of Names, and crash site: it's bisected by a pedestrian walkway that roughly traces the airplane's flight path which, in turn, is lined with tall marble walls that obscure views of the rest of the site. Inside is a permanent exhibition that focuses on the Flight 93 story within the context of the larger terrorist attack.

images.title: File:The Cathedral of Learning, University of Pittsburgh, 5th Avenue and Bigelow Boulevard, Oakland, Pittsburgh, PA.jpg
images.description: Built in 1926-1934, this Gothic Revival-style tower was designed by Charles Klauder to serve as an administration building and classroom building for the University of Pittsburgh.  The building stands 42 stories and 535 feet (163 meters) tall, being the second-tallest university building in the world, only exceeded by the newer Moscow State University Main Building in Russia, and was the second-tallest building in Pittsburgh at the time of its completion, though it lost this status in 1970.  The building is clad in limestone with a massing that tapers towards the top and center with multiple setbacks, a four-story podium at the base with bay windows and tall recessed gothic arched entrance bays, buttresses and tracery on the exterior facade, pinnacles and a parapet with multiple gothic arches at the top of the building, a theater to the southeast of the main building with similar exterior features but a much lower height, known as the Stephen Foster Memorial, and a series of themed classrooms with various decorative finishes inside the building.  The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975, and is a contributing structure in the Schenley Farms Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.  The building today remains the principal structure of the University of Pittsburgh campus, dominating the surrounding Oakland neighborhood, and standing in the middle of a large lawn with trees and smaller buildings at the edges.

images.title: File:Mothman Statue (cropped).jpg
images.description: A photograph of the Mothman Statue and surrounding street in Point Pleasant West Virginia. The statue is large and takes up most of the median, with streets on either side. The Mothman is a cryptid well known in the Midwest for his supposed involvement with the Silver Bridge collapse in Point Pleasant West Virginia, which killed 46 people on December 15, 1967. Sightings of the cryptid had been noted for weeks before the disaster, and many believe he was there to warn the town of the impending disaster. Point Pleasant is now a tourist destination for those interested in cryptids, and a museum has been created to document the sightings and events surrounding the bridge collapse.
